note: Authored source findings precede synthesis. Task-control ratings and feelings of helplessness remain different endpoints. No causal mediator/pathway or operational use authorized.

findings.locator: Europe PMC XML, sections 2.2.1, 4.2.1–4.2.4; 4.1.4 item wording; Discussion limitations
findings.design: Randomized unequal-group task protocol; EC tested first and pseudo-yoked average durations shuffled for YC
findings.population: Healthy German-speaking young adults recruited in Mainz; psychiatric/hearing exclusions
findings.sample: 122 recruited; 100 after completeness/exclusions; two extreme outliers excluded in results (98 for reported control contrast)
findings.context: Repeated aversive-noise button/cue task; not generic life agency
findings.exposure: Button response controls termination under specified protocol
findings.comparator: Response-independent pseudo-yoked termination with otherwise declared task conditions
findings.measurement: 1–7 rating of control over the task, not specifically over the stressor
findings.timing: After each 15-trial block within one session
findings.result: Contingent-response group rated task control higher; effect cannot isolate experienced success, instruction, timing and task contingency as independent components.
findings.limitations: Single task/small healthy sample; unequal groups and session order; pseudo-yoking not person-wise matching; no chronic/control-over-stressor generalization.

findings.locator: Europe PMC XML section 2.1.1; 4.1.4; Discussion paragraph on control-item limitations
findings.design: Three-group initial protocol with escapable, yoked inescapable and no-stressor controls
findings.population: Healthy sample in initial laboratory design
findings.context: Different initial stressor/task design, not exact replication of Study 2
findings.measurement: Same task-control wording, not a measure of objective control
findings.result: Task-control ratings differed in expected order, while many stress/transfer contrasts failed to separate the stress groups.
findings.limitations: Initial protocol differs; group age imbalance and exclusions; do not claim all downstream outcomes improve.

findings.locator: Europe PMC XML sections 2.2.2 and 4.1.4 rating item
findings.measurement: Single 1–7 current feeling-of-helplessness rating, not future action-outcome expectancy
findings.result: Lower reported feelings of helplessness under controllable protocol; exact alignment to PSY-015 expected futility remains insufficient.
findings.limitations: State-feeling/expectancy mismatch, shared self-report, same randomized operation does not identify causal mediation through perceived control.

findings.locator: Europe PMC XML section 2.1.2: EC versus YC helplessness contrast
findings.result: EC versus YC helplessness difference not statistically detected; both stress groups differed from no-stress control.
findings.limitations: No equivalence margin or bounded null; design differs from Study 2; exact canonical expectation construct still unresolved.

assertions.scope: In the specified healthy young-adult aversive-noise task, a response-contingent termination protocol versus its pseudo-yoked noncontingent comparator increased perceived control OVER THAT TASK. Not a universal effect of control availability, not specifically a validated measure of stressor controllability, not chronic agency or psychological safety.
assertions.timing: Within-session repeated task ratings; no persistence estimate
assertions.measurement: Explicit 1–7 perceived control-over-task item. Do not substitute stressor-control, helplessness, behavior, symptoms or objective contingency.
assertions.mechanism: Experienced action/outcome contingency within the assigned protocol informs perceived influence over the task. Multiple protocol features are not separate identified causes.
assertions.rationale: Randomized protocol preceded task-specific control ratings; initial-study results support task-control distinction while mixed downstream readouts remain exclusions, not efficacy claims. Limited strength reflects one publication and narrow population.
assertions.risk: Aversive research exposure is not a recommended action; no permission to impose noise or deception. Consent, ethics, safety, legal authority and feasibility independently required.

assertions.contributionReconciliation: Proxy/possible inverse appraisal overlap with EA-003; research description only, not an independent propagating contribution or identified mediator.
assertions.scope: Research question whether the same contingent-control protocol alters expected ineffectiveness of one's actions (PSY-015). Current evidence measures feelings of helplessness, not the exact expectation; direction remains UNKNOWN.
assertions.timing: Only same-session feeling ratings available; enduring expected futility not established
assertions.measurement: Missing independently aligned expected action-outcome ineffectiveness measure; feeling rating insufficient
assertions.mechanism: Contingency learning is plausible but cannot identify expected futility or mediation from simultaneous task ratings.
assertions.rationale: Source contrasts are preserved without promoting proxy correspondence; Study 1 null versus Study 2 effect does not resolve the construct mismatch.
assertions.risk: Do not infer learned helplessness, depression, chronic harm or treatment benefit; no causal summation with EA-003 and no practitioner eligibility.

happeningTypes.name: Assign a response-contingent termination rule in a bounded aversive-noise task
happeningTypes.description: Configure the declared button/cue protocol so a qualifying response terminates the laboratory noise episode. A researcher operation identity only; no efficacy, ethical permission or real-world stress protection implied. Comparator and session-level variations belong to scoped effects.
happeningTypes.constraints: Exposure safety, consent, ethics review, deception/debriefing, legal authority, accessibility and actor control are not granted by candidate identity. Not interchangeable with speech babble or routine noise exposure.
